newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin stable, complications possible - doctor.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin stable, complications possible - doctor.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin's condition has "stabilised significantly" in the past three days, chief Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov told a news conference.

But he warned that pneumonia, the illness that put Yeltsin in hospital on January 8, was a serious ailment that could involve a range of possible complications which doctors would be monitoring on a daily basis.
"His condition has stabilised to a significant extent in the last three days. His temperature has already been showing normal readings for almost six days," Mironov said.
"But I should say that this is a fairly serious illness, which of course brings with it a whole range of possible complications," he added. "In this respect, there will be a daily doctors' meeting."
Mironov said Yeltsin, 65, should stay in Moscow's Central Clinical Hospital until the end of the week.
Interfax news agency quoted Mironov as saying he expected Yeltsin to be able to attend a summit of leaders of former Soviet states, which is due to take place in Moscow toward the end of January.
